phrases.arabic: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، اِخْلَعْ حِذَاءَكَ عِنْدَ الْبَاب
عَنْ إِذْنِكُمْ، أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَغْسِلَ يَدَيَّ

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَيْنَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَرْكُنَ سَيَّارَتِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. ayna astatee3u an arkuna sayyaaratee?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. Where can I park my car?

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. اُرْكُنْهَا أَمَامَ الْبَيْت، ثُمَّ تَفَضَّلْ بِالدُّخُول.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. urkunhaa amaama al-bayt, thumma tafaddal bid-dukhool.
dialogue.english: And upon you peace. Park it in front of the house, then please come in.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Thanks. I brought you a few simple things.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: Don't trouble yourself, you're at home.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.arabic: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، اِخْلَعْ حِذَاءَكَ عِنْدَ الْبَاب.
dialogue.english: Please take off your shoes at the door.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Of course. Your house is very nice.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: How long did it take you to arrive?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: جَيِّد، وَجَدْتُ الْبَيْتَ بِسُهُولَة. اسْتَغْرَقَتْ نِصْفَ سَاعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: jayyid, wajadtu al-bayta bisuhoola. istaghraqat nisfa saa3a.
dialogue.english: Fine, I found the house easily. It took half an hour.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: عَنْ إِذْنِكَ، أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَغْسِلَ يَدَيَّ.
dialogue.english: Excuse me, I want to wash my hands.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: Of course, the bathroom is on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. لَقَدْ تَكَلَّفْتَ كَثِيرًا مِنْ أَجْلِي.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. laqad takallafta katheeran min ajlee.
dialogue.english: Thanks. You went to a lot of trouble for me.

dialogue.speaker: Faisal
dialogue.english: You have honored us, Ahmad.

pair.english: I brought you a few simple things.
How long did it take you to arrive?
Did you find the house easily?

lessons.culture: A guest is welcomed at the door with أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا, and the host says أَنْتَ فِي بَيْتِكَ, 'you are in your own house'. Bringing a small gift is polite, and the host will usually say you did not need to.

exercises.prompt: Your host says: 'أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا، تَفَضَّلْ بِالدُّخُول'. Thank him.
exercises.tip: شُكْرًا لَكَ is 'thank you' to a man; to a woman it is شُكْرًا لَكِ.

exercises.prompt: Your host says: 'شَرَّفْتَنَا'. Reply modestly.
exercises.tip: بَلْ means 'no, rather' and returns the compliment.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لَا تَتَكَلَّفْ، أَنْتَ فِي _____.' (You're at home.)
exercises.tip: فِي بَيْتِكَ is 'in your house'; the host says it to put you at ease.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، _____ حِذَاءَكَ عِنْدَ الْبَاب.' (Please take off your shoes at the door.)
exercises.tip: اِخْلَعْ is the command 'take off' to a man.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Welcome, please come in.'
exercises.tip: تَفَضَّلْ is the polite 'please, go ahead' to a man.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Where can I park my car?'
exercises.tip: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ is 'I am able to' and is followed by the present verb.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'This house is very nice.'?
exercises.tip: بَيْتُكُمْ is 'your house' said to a family.

exercises.prompt: What does a host say to put a guest at ease?
exercises.tip: تَكَلَّفَ means 'put oneself to trouble'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'بِالدُّخُول / تَفَضَّلْ / وَسَهْلًا، / أَهْلًا'.
exercises.tip: The greeting comes first, then the invitation.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'سَيَّارَتِي؟ / أَسْتَطِيعُ / أَيْنَ / أَنْ / أَرْكُنَ'.
exercises.tip: The question word أَيْنَ opens the sentence.

reply.english: I'd like a glass of tea.

phrases.arabic: اِضْغَطْ عَلَى الْجَرَسِ، لَا بُدَّ أَنَّهُمْ وَصَلُوا
phrases.transliteration: idghat 3alaa al-jarasi, laa budda annahum wasaloo

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Sit down and relax a little, Tariq.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا يَا مُنَى. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran yaa Munaa. baytukum jameelun jiddan.
dialogue.english: Thanks, Mona. Your house is very nice.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: مَاذَا تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَشْرَب؟ قَهْوَةٌ أَمْ شَاي؟
dialogue.transliteration: maadhaa tureedu an tashrab? qahwatun am shaay?
dialogue.english: What would you like to drink? Coffee or tea?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: Tea, please.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Do you take sugar in your tea?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: A little sugar.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: I put the sweets on the table.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: You went to a lot of trouble.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Don't be shy, the house is your house.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: Your kids have grown up so much!

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. شَغِّلِ التِّلْفَازَ إِنْ أَحْبَبْتَ.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, al7amdu lillaah. shaghghili at-tilfaaza in a7babta.
dialogue.english: Yes, thank God. Turn on the TV if you'd like.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: Today's gathering is very nice.

pair.english: What would you like to drink?
Sit down and relax a little.

lessons.culture: A Fusha host offers a drink at once, and the guest is expected to accept something. Phrases such as الْبَيْتُ بَيْتُكَ, 'the house is your house', make the guest feel at ease.

exercises.prompt: Your host asks: 'قَهْوَةٌ أَمْ شَاي؟'. Ask for tea.
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ is 'please', literally 'from your favor'.

exercises.prompt: The host says: 'لَا تَخْجَلْ، الْبَيْتُ بَيْتُك'. Thank him.
exercises.tip: كَرِيم means 'generous', a common compliment for a host.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'قَهْوَةٌ _____ شَاي؟' (Coffee or tea?)
exercises.tip: أَمْ is 'or' in a question that offers a choice.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'اِجْلِسْ وَ_____ قَلِيلًا.' (Sit down and relax a little.)
exercises.tip: اِسْتَرِحْ is the command 'rest' to a man.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'What would you like to drink?'
exercises.tip: تُرِيدُ أَنْ is 'you want to'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Don't be shy, the house is your house.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: لَا plus a short verb form is the negative command.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Take your time, no rush'?
exercises.tip: اِسْتَعْجَلَ means 'hurry'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'sweets'?
exercises.tip: الْحَلْوَى comes from حُلْو, 'sweet'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْبَيْتُ / بَيْتُك / تَخْجَلْ، / لَا'.
exercises.tip: The advice comes first, then the reason.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'شَاي؟ / أَمْ / قَهْوَةٌ'.
exercises.tip: The two choices sit on either side of أَمْ.

phrases.arabic: لَا تَخْجَلْ، قُلْ لِي إِنْ أَرَدْتَ شَيْئًا آخَر
phrases.transliteration: laa takhjal, qul lee in aradta shay2an aakhar

phrases.arabic: اِبْقَ قَلِيلًا، لَمْ نَأْكُلِ الْحَلْوَى بَعْد
phrases.transliteration: ibqa qaleelan, lam na2kuli al-7alwaa ba3d

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.english: Please come to the table, dinner is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Thanks, it smells good.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.english: Try this dish, I made it today.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Masha'Allah, it's delicious.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.english: This food is a bit spicy, be careful.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: No problem, I like spicy food.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.english: Do you want some more bread?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Yes, thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: لَا تَخْجَلْ، قُلْ لِي إِنْ أَرَدْتَ شَيْئًا آخَر.
dialogue.transliteration: laa takhjal, qul lee in aradta shay2an aakhar.
dialogue.english: Don't be shy, tell me if you want anything else.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Thank God, we're full and satisfied.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: اِبْقَ قَلِيلًا، لَمْ نَأْكُلِ الْحَلْوَى بَعْد.
dialogue.transliteration: ibqa qaleelan, lam na2kuli al-7alwaa ba3d.
dialogue.english: Stay a bit, we haven't had dessert yet.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: جَيِّدٌ أَنَّ الطَّعَامَ لَمْ يَبْرُد، وَالْآنَ الْحَلْوَى!
dialogue.transliteration: jayyidun anna at-ta3aama lam yabrud, wal-aana al-7alwaa!
dialogue.english: Good thing the food didn't get cold, and now dessert!

pair.english: What do you think of the dish?
Do you want some more bread?

lessons.culture: Hosts urge guests to eat more, and a guest often refuses once out of politeness before accepting. هَنِيئًا لَكُمْ is said to people who are eating, بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكُمْ is the reply, and ending with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه shows thanks for the meal.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you while you eat: 'هَنِيئًا لَكُمْ'. Reply.
exercises.tip: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكُمْ is the usual blessing in return.

exercises.prompt: The host asks: 'هَلْ تُرِيدُ مَزِيدًا مِنَ الْخُبْز؟'. You are full. Decline politely.
exercises.tip: شَبِعْتُ is 'I am full'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'تَفَضَّلُوا إِلَى _____، الْعَشَاءُ جَاهِز.' (Please come to the table, dinner is ready.)
exercises.tip: الْمَائِدَة is the table set for a meal.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'جَرِّبْ هَذَا _____، أَعْدَدْتُهُ الْيَوْم.' (Try this dish, I made it today.)
exercises.tip: الطَّبَق means both 'plate' and 'dish'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'What do you think of the dish?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: مَا رَأْيُكَ is 'what is your opinion'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Thank God, we're full and satisfied.'
exercises.tip: اِكْتَفَى means 'had enough'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Don't hesitate, eat as you like'?

too_formal.item: لَا تِتْرَدَّد، كُلْ مِثْل مَا بَدَّك

exercises.tip: كُلْ is the command 'eat' to a man.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'dessert'?
exercises.tip: الْخُبْز is bread, الْمَاء water and الْمِلْح salt.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْعَشَاءُ / جَاهِز / الْمَائِدَةِ، / إِلَى / تَفَضَّلُوا'.
exercises.tip: The invitation comes first, then the reason.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْخُبْز؟ / مِنَ / مَزِيدًا / تُرِيدُ / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: مَزِيدًا مِنَ means 'more of'.

phrases.arabic: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَذْهَبَ، لَقَدْ تَأَخَّرَ الْوَقْت
phrases.transliteration: yajibu an nadhhaba, laqad ta2akhkhara al-waqt

phrases.arabic: لَا تَنْسَ أَنَّ بَيْتَنَا بَيْتُكَ دَائِمًا
phrases.transliteration: laa tansa anna baytanaa baytuka daa2iman

phrases.arabic: لَا أَعْذَار، هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ نَفْتَرِقَ بِهَذِهِ السُّرْعَة؟
phrases.transliteration: laa a3dhaar, hal yajibu an naftariqa bihadhihi as-sur3a?

phrases.arabic: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة، قَضَيْنَا وَقْتًا رَائِع
أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ يَكُونَ الطَّرِيقُ خَالِيًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه
phrases.transliteration: atamannaa an yakoona at-tareequ khaaliyan in shaa2a allaah

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Thank you for the hospitality.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: The house is yours, Jamal.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.arabic: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَذْهَبَ، لَقَدْ تَأَخَّرَ الْوَقْت.
dialogue.transliteration: yajibu an nadhhaba, laqad ta2akhkhara al-waqt.
dialogue.english: We need to go, it's gotten late.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.arabic: لَا أَعْذَار، هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ نَفْتَرِقَ بِهَذِهِ السُّرْعَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa a3dhaar, hal yajibu an naftariqa bihadhihi as-sur3a?
dialogue.english: No excuses, do we have to part so quickly?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة، قَضَيْنَا وَقْتًا رَائِع.
dialogue.english: Thanks for the invitation, we had a great time.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: A very nice gathering, God keep you.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Give my regards to the family.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه. لَا تَنْسَ أَنَّ بَيْتَنَا بَيْتُكَ دَائِمًا.
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2a allaah. laa tansa anna baytanaa baytuka daa2iman.
dialogue.english: God willing. Don't forget our house is always your house.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Let us know when you get home.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.arabic: بِالتَّأْكِيد. أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ يَكُونَ الطَّرِيقُ خَالِيًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.
dialogue.transliteration: bit-ta2keed. atamannaa an yakoona at-tareequ khaaliyan in shaa2a allaah.
dialogue.english: Of course. The road should be clear, God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Visit us again soon.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Goodbye, God be with you.

pair.english: Give my regards to the family.

lessons.culture: Leaving a Fusha home takes time: the guest says they must go, the host insists they stay, and both exchange prayers such as فِي أَمَانِ اللَّه, 'in God's safekeeping'. Asking a guest to send word on reaching home shows care.

exercises.prompt: You are leaving. Thank the host for the invitation.
exercises.tip: الدَّعْوَة is 'the invitation'.

exercises.prompt: The host says: 'مَعَ السَّلَامَة'. Reply.
exercises.tip: فِي أَمَانِ اللَّه is a blessing for the traveler.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'سَلِّمْ لِي عَلَى _____.' (Give my regards to the family.)
exercises.tip: سَلِّمْ لِي عَلَى is 'greet for me'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'يَجِبُ أَنْ نَذْهَبَ، لَقَدْ _____ الْوَقْت.' (We need to go, it's gotten late.)
exercises.tip: تَأَخَّرَ الْوَقْت is 'the time has become late'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Thanks for the invitation, we had a great time.'
exercises.answer: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة، قَضَيْنَا وَقْتًا رَائِع
accepted: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة، قَضَيْنَا وَقْتًا رَائِع
شكرا على الدعوة، قضينا وقتا رائعا
exercises.tip: قَضَى وَقْتًا is 'spent time'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Visit me again soon.'
exercises.tip: زُرْنِي is 'visit me'; مَرَّةً أُخْرَى is 'another time'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Let us know when you get home'?
exercises.tip: عِنْدَمَا means 'when' and is followed by a verb.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase is a parting blessing meaning 'in God's safekeeping'?
exercises.tip: أَمَان is 'safety'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'مَرَّةً / قَرِيبًا / أُخْرَى / زُرْنِي'.
exercises.tip: The command comes first, then how often, then when.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'السَّلَامَة، / مَعَ / اللَّه / أَمَانِ / فِي'.
exercises.tip: The plain goodbye comes first, then the blessing.

challenge.title: Host and thank a guest
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which a guest arrives at a friend's home, is welcomed and offered a drink, sits down to eat, praises the food, and says thanks and goodbye before leaving.
required_elements: an invitation to the table and a compliment on the food

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Welcome, please come in.

dialogue.speaker: Lubna
dialogue.english: Thank you. Your house is very nice.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Sit down and relax. Coffee or tea?

dialogue.speaker: Lubna
dialogue.english: Tea, please.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Please come to the table, dinner is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Lubna
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللَّه، الطَّعَامُ لَذِيذٌ جِدًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a allaah, at-ta3aamu ladheedhun jiddan.
dialogue.english: Masha'Allah, the food is delicious.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: Enjoy. Would you like some more?

dialogue.speaker: Lubna
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا، شَبِعْتُ. جَزَاكُمُ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا عَلَى الضِّيَافَة.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, shabi3tu. jazaakumu allaahu khayran 3alaa ad-diyaafa.
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'm full. Thank you for the hospitality.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.english: The house is yours. Visit us soon.

dialogue.speaker: Lubna
dialogue.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه. مَعَ السَّلَامَة، فِي أَمَانِ اللَّه.
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2a allaah. ma3a as-salaama, fee amaani allaah.
dialogue.english: God willing. Goodbye, God be with you.
